newsitem.title: UK: Dassault seeks speedy Aerospatiale merger.
newsitem.headline: Dassault seeks speedy Aerospatiale merger.

text.p: A planned merger between combat plane maker Dassault Aviation and state-owned SNI Aerospatiale should go ahead as fast as possible, as the present air of uncertainty weighs on Dassault's commercial prospects.

But Bruno Revellin-Falcoz, deputy chairman of Dassault, told reporters on Sunday night ahead of the Farnborough airshow that he could not set a timetable for completing the merger as there were complex evaluation and legal procedures involved.

"I do not know when the date for completion will be, as there are many questions which must be answered," he said. "But everything will be done on our side so that things do not drag as periods of uncertainty are not healthy, particularly on the commercial front."

Chairman Serge Dassault was unable to host the traditional dinner for the French media on the eve of the air show, as there is an international arrest warrant for him from the Belgian police in connection with an inquiry into alleged corruption on a defence contract.
Revellin-Falcoz said he thought a deadline fixed by the French government for submission of proposals for the merger terms by end-December would be met.
"We have an objective set by the government...I think we will meet it," he said.

An evaluation of assets of the two companies was under way and the results would be known in "the coming weeks and months", he said. The percentage that Serge Dassault would hold in the new merged company would only be known when this process was completed.

He welcomed news of the improving finances of Aerospatiale announced by chairman Yves Michot over the weekend, saying: "We welcome with great pleasure the improvement in the Aerospatiale situation. We have accepted a merger with Aerospatiale to create a strong group."
